points.t: **One larger oval patch**, then 1–2 weeks later many smaller pink ovals with a **collarette** on the trunk.
Probably **HHV-6 / HHV-7 reactivation**; not contagious in practice.
Explain and reassure; emollients, mild–moderate steroid or antihistamine for itch; review if > 12 weeks.
**Secondary syphilis** (palms / soles, mucosa, nodes), guttate psoriasis, tinea, drug eruption; **PR in early pregnancy**.

cause.lead: A viral-style eruption with a predictable course.
points: Ages 10–35; may follow a URTI-like prodrome.
Strongest evidence: **HHV-6 / HHV-7** reactivation; recurrence only ~2–3%.
**Pityriasiform drug eruptions** (ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, isotretinoin, some biologics / vaccines): no herald patch, persist on the drug.

features.lead: Herald patch, then the Christmas tree.
points: **Herald patch**: single 2–5 cm oval salmon-pink plaque, fine **collarette scale inside the edge**.
**Secondary eruption** after ~1–2 weeks: smaller ovals along skin lines → **‘Christmas tree’** on back, ‘V’ on chest.
Spares face, scalp, palms, soles. Itch: none to moderate (~25% significant).
Variants: **inverse** (flexural), papular, vesicular, purpuric. Darker skin: grey-brown / violaceous; prolonged pigment change.

points: If atypical, **palms / soles**, no herald patch, sexual risk, or > 12 weeks.
If the herald patch alone looks like tinea.

cards.name: Guttate psoriasis
cards.clue: Many small drop papules, thicker silvery scale, **no herald patch**, after strep throat.

cards.name: Secondary syphilis
cards.clue: Palms / soles, mucous patches, nodes, malaise; positive serology.

cards.name: Tinea corporis
cards.clue: Active scaly edge, central clearing; KOH +.

cards.name: Pityriasiform drug eruption
cards.clue: New drug, no herald patch, persists.

points: Benign, **non-contagious**, settles in 6–12 weeks; no isolation; no scarring (pigment may linger).
Emollients, soap substitutes; avoid hot showers, perfumes, tight clothes; moderate sun may help.
**Mild–moderate topical steroid** (e.g. clobetasone butyrate 0.05%) short course; sedating antihistamine at night or non-sedating by day.
High-dose aciclovir early in extensive disease: limited evidence, specialist decision.

limits.t: Don’t: may prolong or worsen PR.

items.t: Palm / sole lesions, mouth ulcers, nodes or sexual risk: **syphilis serology** and sexual health.
PR in the **first 15 weeks of pregnancy**: inform midwife / obstetric team.

pearls.t: ‘One big patch, then many small ovals along the ribs’ = PR; ‘shower of drops after strep throat’ = guttate psoriasis.
Every generalised papulosquamous rash: **sexual history + look at palms and soles**.
Herald patch often mistreated as ringworm: antifungal failure is a clue.

quiz.q: Where is the scale on a herald patch?
quiz.a: A collarette just inside the edge (tinea: at the advancing edge).
Atypical, palms / soles, no herald patch, sexual risk, or > 12 weeks.
Inform the midwife / obstetric team (miscarriage risk).
